bugs.name: Generated pull request references and activity avatars use unreachable localhost URLs
bugs.summary: Gitea generates absolute URLs with https://localhost:5503 in user-facing merge commit references and activity avatars on the Daytona site. The localhost pull request links cannot be opened from the hosted app, and contributor avatars fail to load.
bugs.expected: Generated links and avatar image URLs should use the hosted site's reachable origin so users can open pull request references and see contributor avatars.
bugs.actual: A merged pull request's commit shows Reviewed-on #3 linking to https://localhost:5503/admin/D-from-template/pulls/3; clicking the corresponding localhost reference in another merged PR led to a browser connection error. The Activity > Pulse contributor avatar in admin/D-from-template uses https://localhost:5503/avatars/51965088c5db83c3fd307f308d25198a and renders broken with ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED.
reproSteps: On a hosted fixture, sign in as eval and create and merge a pull request.
Open the merge commit and inspect its Reviewed-on pull-request link.
Open Activity → Pulse and inspect contributor avatar URLs.
Observe URLs using https://localhost:5503 rather than the hosted fixture origin.
bugs.reason: Human review rejected this as a Gitea product bug. The unreachable localhost URLs are a fixture/configuration issue; correct the instance public URL instead of scoring this claim as a product defect.

bugs.name: All Branches commit history omits docs/release-owners-only commit
bugs.summary: Selecting All Branches leaves the commit history at the single main-branch commit, while comparison confirms a distinct commit on docs/release-owners.
bugs.expected: With All Branches selected, the history should include commits from all repository branches, including the commit unique to docs/release-owners.
bugs.actual: The selected filter remained visibly set to All Branches, but after waiting the history still showed 1 commit: “Add engineering handbook and release checklist.” The compare page for main..docs/release-owners showed the separate “Document release captain and verification responsibilities” commit.
reproSteps: Start signed in to the Gitea test account eval (the supplied authenticated session was already active; no credentials were entered).
Open /eval/harbor-handbook/commits/branch/main.
Open the commit-scope dropdown, currently showing This Branch, and select All Branches.
Wait six seconds. Observe the selected All Branches filter, the 1 Commits count, and the only row, “Add engineering handbook and release checklist.”
Open /eval/harbor-handbook/compare/main..docs/release-owners and observe the distinct “Document release captain and verification responsibilities” commit.
bugs.reason: User rejected the claim because All Branches selects the scope of a commit-message search; it is not an immediately applied history filter. The recording changes only the scope dropdown without submitting a query. An independent normal-UI control submitted responsibilities with All Branches and found the docs/release-owners commit; the same query limited to This Branch returned no commits.

bugs.name: Code search matched line-number link does not open the source line
bugs.summary: The matched README.md line-number link for line 8 leaves code search unchanged instead of opening the source at that line.
bugs.expected: Clicking matched line 8 in README.md opens that file at line 8.
bugs.actual: After two successful clicks on the displayed line-number link and a five-second wait, the browser remained on the same search URL and the search results were unchanged.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open the seeded eval/harbor-handbook repository’s code-search page.
Enter issue, choose Regexp and submit the visible search form.
In the README.md result, click the actual line-number 8 link, rather than the code text or surrounding table cell.
Observe navigation to the correct commit’s README.md#L8. Use browser Back and click View file as a separate navigation control.
bugs.reason: User-approved rejection of the reported no-navigation failure. The recorded no-op clicks targeted the surrounding table cell, not the anchor. Independent actual-browser checks, including a fresh fixture control, clicked the line-number link and opened the correct README. View file also worked.

matchingGuidance.scope: Reject the claim that clicking the actual link leaves search unchanged. Rendered Markdown does not automatically reveal or highlight source line 8; the live control needed View Source followed by clicking 8 to show that highlight. This rejection does not adjudicate that narrower Markdown line-targeting behavior.

bugs.name: Markdown editor Preview does not render bold emphasis for unsaved text
bugs.summary: The unsaved Markdown Preview correctly renders a heading but displays **Preview paragraph.** as regular-weight text instead of bold.
bugs.expected: On the unsaved .md edit, Preview Changes should show the replacement diff, and Preview should render “# Preview heading” as a heading and “**Preview paragraph.**” as bold text without committing the edit.
bugs.actual: Preview Changes showed the expected replacement diff. Preview rendered “Preview heading” as a heading but rendered “Preview paragraph.” in regular weight. The state remained unchanged after loading, and the edit was not committed.
reproSteps: Start at /eval/harbor-handbook in the supplied authenticated browser session; verify the UI shows the signed-in account as eval. No sign-in form or credential variables were used.
Use the branch selector to create the fresh branch qa-verify76-preview-bold-20260522 from main.
Choose Add File > New File. Create qa-verify76-preview-bold-20260522.md with “# Original heading”, a blank line, and “Existing paragraph.”; commit this baseline fixture directly to the branch.
Open the new file and choose Edit. The observed edit URL is /eval/harbor-handbook/_edit/qa-verify76-preview-bold-20260522/qa-verify76-preview-bold-20260522.md.
Replace the contents with “# Preview heading”, a blank line, and “**Preview paragraph.**”.
Choose Preview Changes and confirm the displayed diff contains the unsaved replacement.
Choose Preview. Observe the heading rendered as a heading and the paragraph rendered in regular weight, not bold. Leave the edit uncommitted.
bugs.reason: User explicitly rejected the reported absence of bold as a hallucination: the text is bold. The original native recording contains valid **Preview paragraph.** input and a rendered strong element. Independent UI inspection confirms strong uses the intended weight 600 while normal paragraph text uses 400. The evidence does not establish missing Markdown formatting.

matchingGuidance.scope: Reject the claim that this editor failed to render bold Markdown. This does not label unrelated Markdown parsing or preview-persistence failures as intended behavior.

bugs.name: Commit search leaves unrelated commits visible for a specific matching query
bugs.summary: Commit search for "Document release captain" also returns "Add engineering handbook and release checklist".
bugs.expected: Only commits matching the full phrase appear.
bugs.actual: Both commits appear because each matches at least one query word.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open eval/harbor-handbook, branch docs/release-owners.
Open commit history and search for "Document release captain".
bugs.reason: Works as intended: commit search uses word-based OR matching. The second commit matches "release"; full-phrase matching is not required.

bugs.name: Commit history no-match search shows Go formatting artifacts
bugs.summary: Searching commit history for a term with no matches exposes Go formatting artifacts and an unrelated histories message.
bugs.expected: A search with no matching commits should show a clear empty state without template artifacts.
bugs.actual: Searching commit history for a term with no matches exposes Go formatting artifacts and an unrelated histories message.
reproSteps: Open an authenticated repository and its Commits history.
Enter `no-such-commit-term-xyz` in Search commits and submit.
Observe the malformed no-results message above the populated search field.
bugs.reason: Rejected for the pinned Gitea 1.24.7 fixture (source commit 99053ce4fa2b45f1bca5837418c0c57f793ca824): SearchCommits sets PageIsCommits and renders the commit-count branch, not the unrelated-histories translation that needs branch arguments. Searching the seeded main history for no-such-commit-term-xyz displayed 0 Commits and a clean empty area without Go formatting artifacts.

bugs.name: Commit history search leaves nonmatching commit visible
bugs.summary: Searching the docs/release-owners commit history for “Document release captain” leaves both commits visible, including the nonmatching “Add engineering handbook and release checklist.”
bugs.expected: Submitting the query “Document release captain” in the commit history should narrow the results to the matching commit, “Document release captain and verification responsibilities.”
bugs.actual: After submitting with Enter and again with the search button, the query remained in the field and both commits remained visible for at least six seconds, including “Add engineering handbook and release checklist.”
reproSteps: Load the provided saved administrator session; the browser shows the admin account signed in. No credentials were entered.
Navigate to /admin/harbor-handbook.
In the Code tab, open the branch selector and choose docs/release-owners.
Click the branch's “2 Commits” history link.
Type “Document release captain” into the “Search commits...” field and press Enter. Observe that both commits remain visible.
Click the search button, wait six seconds, and observe that both commits still remain visible, including “Add engineering handbook and release checklist.”
bugs.reason: The local reviewed evidence documents word-based OR commit search: the extra commit matches release in Document release captain. The assignment borrows a full-phrase/subject-exclusive search promise the product does not make. This exact observed result is intended under the recorded search contract; choose not_a_bug, independent of duplicate status.

bugs.name: Repository commit count link disappears from the Code page after a second upload commit
bugs.summary: The report claims that after a second commit that uploads new files, the commit count link above the branch selector disappears from the repository's Code page, leaving only the branch and tag counts.
bugs.expected: The reporter expects the commit count link to stay visible in the repository statistics bar.
bugs.actual: After a second upload commit, the statistics bar shows only '1 Branch' and '0 Tags'; the commit count link is gone.
reproSteps: In a repository with an initial commit, use Add File > Upload File to commit new files.
Open the repository's Code page and look at the statistics bar above the branch selector.
bugs.reason: Not reproduced: after an upload commit the statistics bar still shows the commit count link alongside the branch and tag counts, and the code always renders it from the cached count. What can happen is that the count is briefly stale until the cache refreshes, which is a different symptom covered by the commit-count cache entries.

matchingGuidance.scope: Only reports that the commit count link is missing from the Code page. Reports that the count shows an old number after a new commit are not covered here.

bugs.name: Renaming a nested file saves a concatenated root filename
bugs.summary: Replacing contributing.md with contributing-renamed.md in the editor filename field saved docscontributing-renamed.mdcontributing.md at the repository root instead of the requested filename in docs.
bugs.expected: The file is renamed to docs/contributing-renamed.md with original contents retained.
bugs.actual: Saved path is docscontributing-renamed.mdcontributing.md at the repository root. Original contents remain.
reproSteps: On a disposable branch, open docs/contributing.md and choose Edit File.
Replace the filename text with contributing-renamed.md using select-all and typing.
Commit and inspect the resulting path.
bugs.reason: User rejected this reported select-all-and-typing rename claim after being told independent verdicts and the exact editing trigger were unverified. The accepted Backspace-on-selected-filename folder-merging defect remains valid and is explicitly outside this rejection. No independent non-reproduction or intended-behavior conclusion is claimed.

matchingGuidance.scope: Narrowly covers this unverified select-all-and-typing report. Do not apply this negative reference to a confirmed Backspace-triggered folder/filename merge.

relatedReference.distinction: The accepted reference explicitly involves Backspace with the filename selected. That trigger was not established in this rejected report.

reviewEvidence.basis: Explicit user rejection; independent verification pending at decision.
limitations: The rejection is a human labeling decision, not a demonstrated non-reproduction.
Original editing keystrokes and overlap with the accepted Backspace defect remain unverified.

bugs.name: Exact code search is case-sensitive for multi-word queries (single words are case-insensitive)
bugs.summary: The report says that repository code search in Exact mode matches single words regardless of case (for example RELEASE finds Release) but matches multi-word phrases only when the case is exact.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that Exact mode handles case the same way for single words and phrases, so 'release checklist' finds 'Release checklist'.
bugs.actual: Exact mode was case-sensitive for both: 'Harbor' and 'Harbor Ledger' matched, while 'harbor', 'HARBOR', 'RELEASE' and 'harbor ledger' found nothing. The default (Fuzzy) mode matched regardless of case.
reproSteps: Open a repository's code search and choose Exact.
Search for a single word and a phrase from a file, each in different case from the file.
Repeat in the default search mode and compare.
bugs.reason: Not a bug: there's no single-word/phrase difference. Exact mode always searches case-sensitively for the literal text, however many words it has, while the default Fuzzy mode always ignores case; matching the exact term is what the Exact option's tooltip describes. A single word appearing to match case-insensitively most likely came from a search in the default mode.

bugs.name: Uploading a same-named file replaces it after Commit Changes
bugs.summary: The report expects another collision warning when committing an upload with the same name as an existing repository file.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is an additional confirmation or diff before replacing the file.
bugs.actual: After the explicit Commit Changes action, a new Git commit contains the uploaded replacement.
reproSteps: Create and commit a file on a writable branch.
Choose Add File > Upload File and select another file with the same name.
Click Commit Changes and inspect the new file and commit history.
bugs.reason: The reported operation requires explicit Commit Changes and creates a Git commit containing the replacement; the previous file remains in history. No promise of an additional collision confirmation or unintended save is established. The absence of a second warning alone does not prove a functional defect.

bugs.name: File line count includes a trailing empty line omitted from rendering
bugs.summary: The report expects the file and blame line-count header to equal the number of rendered rows for a newline-terminated file.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that a final newline contributes no extra editor-style line.
bugs.actual: The header counts the final empty line while the source rendering omits that empty row.
reproSteps: Open the source or blame view of a newline-terminated file.
Compare its line-count header with the rendered row count.
bugs.reason: Pinned source explicitly defines a newline-terminated a\n as two editor-style lines and says the final empty line is counted but not rendered. The reported discrepancy is exactly the documented behavior.

bugs.name: Repository file tree cannot be navigated with the keyboard
bugs.summary: The Files sidebar renders file and directory entries as nonfocusable div/span elements, preventing keyboard users from selecting files or expanding directories. Verified on both seeded main and the test branch.
bugs.expected: File entries should be keyboard-focusable links or treeitems, and directories should support keyboard expansion with appropriate accessible roles.
bugs.actual: All sidebar entries are exposed as static text and skipped by keyboard focus. Files can be selected with a mouse but cannot be reached or activated using the keyboard.
reproSteps: Open /eval/harbor-handbook/src/branch/main/docs/releases.md with the Files sidebar visible.
Tab to the Hide file tree button.
Press Tab: focus jumps past all file and directory entries directly to the main branch selector.
Try reaching a tree item with Tab/Shift+Tab: none is focusable. The rendered tree has zero links, buttons, or tabindex elements.
bugs.reason: Excluded by the browser bug-reproducer pure-accessibility rule. This report establishes only keyboard/focus/accessibility semantics or a generic contrast threshold, without an explicit supplied product requirement or documented promise for that behavior. Ordinary pointer functionality or visible setting values are not alleged to fail. This negative reference is scoped to the reported accessibility-only claim; it does not cover independently demonstrated data loss, pointer failures, or an explicitly documented keyboard action.

matchingGuidance.distinction: Match only this accessibility/keyboard/contrast claim. Independently observed pointer or saved-data failures, and explicitly promised keyboard shortcuts, are outside this negative reference.

bugs.name: Copy content control cannot be reached by keyboard
bugs.summary: The file viewer's Copy content icon is an anchor with no href, role, or tabindex. Tab navigation skips it, blocking the copy action for keyboard users.
bugs.expected: Copy content should be exposed as a named button that receives keyboard focus and activates with Enter/Space.
bugs.actual: The control is absent from the interactive accessibility snapshot and skipped in both Tab directions. Browser DOM inspection confirms <a aria-label='Copy content'> has no href, role, or tabindex attribute.
reproSteps: Open /eval/harbor-handbook/src/branch/main/README.md.
Press Shift+Tab: focus returns to Download file, again skipping Copy content. Verified both directions.
bugs.reason: Excluded by the browser bug-reproducer pure-accessibility rule. This report establishes only keyboard/focus/accessibility semantics or a generic contrast threshold, without an explicit supplied product requirement or documented promise for that behavior. Ordinary pointer functionality or visible setting values are not alleged to fail. This negative reference is scoped to the reported accessibility-only claim; it does not cover independently demonstrated data loss, pointer failures, or an explicitly documented keyboard action.

matchingGuidance.distinction: Match only this accessibility/keyboard/contrast claim. Independently observed pointer or saved-data failures, and explicitly promised keyboard shortcuts, are outside this negative reference.

bugs.name: Searching from a non-default branch silently searches the default branch
bugs.summary: The repository's code search discards the branch being browsed and gives misleading no-match results for content present on that branch.
bugs.expected: Search the currently selected branch and show the matching docs/releases.md lines, or clearly disclose and allow changing the branch being searched.
bugs.actual: The app navigates to /eval/harbor-handbook/search?q=captain and says "No matching results found" with no indication that the selected branch was discarded. The search uses the default branch instead.
reproSteps: Open a non-default repository branch containing text absent from the default branch.
Submit that text through the repository Search code field.
Inspect the default-branch search results.
bugs.reason: The pinned repository search handler deliberately chooses the default branch (or first existing branch), independently of the currently browsed branch. Its code comment states that scope explicitly; the indexer also indexes the default branch. The report supplies no branch-scoped search promise. Reject the expectation that the generic repository Search code field automatically follows the browsed branch, not separately missing results from the supported default-branch search.

limitations: Source/contract review of the reported behavior; no fresh reproduction or independent judge run.

bugs.name: Commit search is assumed to search authors without the author prefix
bugs.summary: The report searches bare author names and treats missing matches as a broken author search.
bugs.expected: The reporter expects a bare name such as Alex to match the commit author even when absent from the commit message.
bugs.actual: Bare author-name searches return no commits, while matching commit-message terms and SHA prefixes work.
reproSteps: Open a repository commit history with commits by a known author.
Search a bare author-name term that is absent from the commit messages.
Observe no results and compare with a matching commit-message term or SHA prefix.
bugs.reason: The user-facing search tooltip explicitly documents author: and committer: prefixes. NewSearchCommitsOptions puts bare terms in Keywords, which searchCommits passes to git log --grep for commit messages; author: terms instead become --author constraints. The reported bare-keyword behavior follows the supported search contract. This rejection excludes failures with the documented author: syntax.

reviewEvidence.limitations: No new live author-prefix control; the UI tooltip and pinned parser establish the reported input contract.
